claim: Program comprehension theories describe hypothesis-driven top-down reading (Brooks) and bottom-up chunking (Pennington, Letovsky), and experts switch between them as cues allow. Only the 1995 review was read, not the 1983 originals.
agent_test: Run the agent with an explicit hypothesis list before reading code versus read-then-summarise, same token cap, on bug localisation items.

claim: Experts build richer situation (domain) models than novices; situation-model questions are answered better than program-model questions by everyone (4.36 vs 3.55 of 6, N about 46).
agent_test: Require the agent to write a function-purpose statement before proposing a fix; compare fix accuracy at equal tokens.

claim: Novices read code more linearly than experts (about 70-80% linear eye moves vs about 60%, N=20, Busjahn 2015). A non-exact replication (12 novices, 19 intermediates) found the story-order difference between experience groups not reproduced, and that the linearity of the code itself matters more than reader experience; Peachock found no experience effect.
agent_test: Compare linear top-to-bottom reading versus cue-first reading (signatures, names, call sites) for the agent on defect-finding items.

claim: Beacons (meaningful names) speed up comprehension and misleading names hurt, but fMRI/behaviour tests found no beacon-layout effect on four semantic-cue conditions (N=11).
agent_test: Rename identifiers to misleading versus neutral versus original on the same bugs; measure agent accuracy drop.

claim: LLMs over-trust identifier names: misleading names cut code-completion Pass@1 by 17-34% relative and drop document selection from 92.8% to 52.4% (GPT-3.5); reasoning-tuned models track human difficulty under obfuscation, coder-tuned ones do not.
agent_test: Add a name-blind check step (restate behaviour from the code body only) and measure recovery on misleading-name items.

claim: Human attention and LLM attention to code agree poorly: only 22% of methods show significant correlation, and alignment does not predict summary quality (rho -0.13, p=0.39); LLM-vs-LLM agreement is 85%.
agent_test: Do not build schema steps that assume model attention equals human attention; test only by outcome, not by alignment.

claim: Programmer-attention signals injected into code LLMs give small gains: BLEU-4 +1 to +2 points (EyeLayer), up to +7.16 CodeBLEU (single seed), all 36 cells positive (EyeMulator). Training-based, not scaffold-based.
agent_test: Out of scope for a no-training scaffold; instead test a prompt that lists the lines a human reader would fixate (signature, return, comments).

claim: Chain-of-thought and hypothesis-revise loops raise code-execution reasoning a lot: CRUXEval GPT-4 output 63 to 81.9 with CoT; RHDA 68.75 to 90.62 on CRUXEval and 41.18 to 84.16 on LiveCodeBench for GPT-4o. CoT does not help weaker models on input prediction.
agent_test: Equal-token comparison: direct answer versus trace-then-answer versus hypothesise-test-amend on code reasoning items.

claim: Models are fragile to meaning-preserving changes: single mutations cost up to 7-8 points; up to 60.9% of correct answers carry flawed reasoning; CodeMMLU accuracy shifts when option order is permuted; EquiBench best is 82.3% overall but 63.8% on hardest categories. UPDATE (gap search): in Orvalho & Kwiatkowska v3 the flawed-but-correct share is 10-50% for code-tuned open models (Llama3.2 55.1%) but 0.2% for GPT-5.2 and Gemini-3; frontier models still lose up to 70 points under loop unrolling (possible contamination and length effects).
agent_test: Check agent answers under a rewritten but equivalent snippet (consistency check) before commit; measure flip rate.

claim: Real-code semantic reasoning remains weak: CodeSense single C statements under 30% for Claude 3.5 and GPT-4o-mini; input prediction about 12%; few-shot raises R1-Distill-14B from 0.316 to 0.784.
agent_test: Add worked trace examples to prompt versus none; measure on statement-level value prediction.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-03 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Structured repository navigation beats free search: file-centered scaffolds raise Function Acc@5 from 32.61 to 52.13; fewer tools did better than more (7B IoU 24.28 with jump only vs 13.71 with four tools); RL gave 15.46 to 26.43. Gap search: Agentless hierarchical localisation beats skipping levels (SWE-bench Lite, GPT-4o era); not tested on repos larger than SWE-bench or on current frontier agents.
agent_test: Compare coarse-to-fine (tree, file, function) navigation scaffold with unconstrained search at equal tokens.

claim: AI help raises speed but not comprehension: Copilot cut time 50.7% (632 vs 1281 s), comprehension unchanged (7.86 vs 7.27 of 15, p=0.59, N=15); high-comprehension users wrote then viewed code 4.7x as often.
agent_test: Have the agent predict before reading output (write-then-view) and measure fix correctness.

claim: People over-trust generated code: correct assertions judged correct 74%, incorrect judged incorrect 49%, with equal confidence (N=86); 19.3% of students thought they understood but answered at most one question right. Gap search: model-side analogues exist (self-correction blind spot 41-65%, verifier blind spot 0.12-0.55, self-repair gains vanish at equal budget) but they are math/QA mostly and not a direct mirror of the human 49% figure.
agent_test: Test an agent self-check that forces a refutation attempt on its own claim before accepting; measure false-accept rate.

claim: Comprehension experiments are weakly comparable: 95 studies, median N=34, 53.7% students only, 71 of 94 one-factor, measures rarely agree; anchoring on shown complexity shifts ratings (d=-1.29, N=43) but not correctness.
agent_test: Treat all human effect sizes here as weak priors; require own benchmark at equal tokens.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-03 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Atoms of confusion (precedence, side-effect patterns) raise human error 2.7 to 56 times for 7 of 14 Java atoms (N=132, pooled OR 3.82); an EEG study found LLM perplexity tracks human confusion (r=0.45).
agent_test: Run the agent on atom-bearing versus clean snippet pairs; require explicit evaluation-order trace for flagged atoms.

claim: Classic complexity metrics predict comprehension weakly: McCabe near 0, Halstead and LOC small-to-medium (tau 0.1-0.5, N=19).
agent_test: Do not use cyclomatic complexity as a routing signal for agent effort; test token-length or LOC instead.

claim: Review comprehension episodes start with context building then inspection (23 of 25 reviews, 10 reviewers); in a LLM think-aloud, 31 of 50 responses were top-down (docstring first).
agent_test: Force a context-building step (read description, signatures) before inspection; compare with inspection-first.

claim: A hypothesis-first, scientific-debugging scaffold (AutoSD) did not raise repair accuracy over direct LLM patching (Defects4J v1.2: 76 vs 87; v2.0: 113 vs 110) but real debugger execution mattered (73% vs 63% plausible runs) and explanations improved human patch-judging on 5 of 6 bugs. Tested only on 2023 models.
agent_test: Same agent, same token cap: hypothesis-list-first vs read-first on bug localisation with a frontier reasoning model; log whether predicted-then-executed beats predicted-only.

claim: Models are poor at catching errors in their own output: 14 open models show a 64.5% blind spot (Claude Sonnet 4 41.4%) on injected errors; self-repair on code beats resampling at equal budget rarely; a separate verifier of similar strength waves through 12-55% of wrong answers. A cheap 'Wait' trigger removes about 89% of the gap for non-reasoning models, so reasoning models absorb it.
agent_test: Compare self-review of own patch vs review of the same patch labelled as written by someone else, same tokens, on SWE-bench Verified; check false-accept rates.

claim: Consistency across meaning-preserving rewrites is a cheap fragility signal but not shown to be a working verifier: only a union upper bound was measured, frontier models lose 28-70 points under loop rewrites, and a rename helped weak models while hurting Gemini-3 (100 to 68.1).
agent_test: Run the agent on original and 2 rewrites; accept only if answers agree; measure precision and cost vs a single run.

claim: Explaining code line by line before judging it (rubber duck) gives small gains for LLMs (+2-3% Spider, up to +12% with unit tests, matches 10x sampling), but the human write-then-view effect (4.7x) has no direct LLM test.
agent_test: Require the agent to write predicted behaviour before running or viewing code, then compare accuracy at equal tokens.

claim: Localisation accuracy tracks resolve rate across six SWE-bench Verified agents (file-level hits 448 vs 342; ranking by F1 matches ranking by resolve rate), so locate-type episodes are the ones to log and score; no study validated Letovsky-style episode labels on agent traces.
agent_test: Hand-label 50 agent traces with read/ask-why/conjecture/simulate/verify, measure inter-rater kappa and correlation with success.
